title: Allow Sort
statement: Implement `solve(choice, allowed)`. `allowed` maps a client sort key to a real column name. Return the column name when `choice` is a key. Return `error` when it is not. Do not return `choice` itself unless the mapping says so.
constraints: The mapped column is the SQL fragment
hints: A hit returns the column, which may differ from the key.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: ORDER BY cannot take a bound parameter for the column name.

editorial: ORDER BY cannot take a bound parameter for the column name. Interpolating the client's string is injection. An allow-list maps a public key to a column you wrote. Anything else is rejected. The mapped name is what you would splice in.
